_comment: SCRATCH FIXTURE, and the answer to 'how many doors can one lever gate?'. Thirty-six switch tiles and ONE lever: nine two-tile 'A' gates standing in the corridor the route walks (columns 4,6,8,10,12,14,16,18,20 at rows 11-12) and the nine matching two-tile 'a' gates in the sealed chamber above (rows 8-9), which are the same nine doors in their other configuration. All thirty-six resolve off the same two booleans in TileWorld.switch_states, so throwing the one lever at (2,12) opens every gate on the route and shuts every gate above it, in the same frame, at no cost that grows with N -- TileWorld.is_solid() asks data.switch_group[id] per tile and there is no registry, no cap and no per-screen limit anywhere in the chain. What a level CANNOT have is a third independent gate: data/tiles.json defines groups 1 and 2 and nothing else, ProverSim packs the world's switch state into two bits, and every switch_a in a level is group 1 -- so a second 'a' lever anywhere in the level undoes the first. Kept in tests/fixtures/ and out of levels/ -- it is an experiment, not a level.
name: SWITCH FAN-OUT
